data.narrative:
Innoviz Technologies (INVZ) is a public-stage company operating in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The comparable universe consists of five private peers within the same sector—Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air—with no direct public comparables identified. The absence of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with sufficient valuation overlap constrains traditional peer-multiple triangulation.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable in this instance. While five same-sector peers exist, none met the filtering criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier necessary to produce a reliable cohort of three or more datapoints. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable comparability noise, given the heterogeneity of business models, maturity, and capital intensity across the Drones & Autonomous landscape.

This analysis indicates that conventional multiple-based valuation for Innoviz is structurally limited by peer set constraints. Alternative methods—such as precedent transaction analysis within autonomous systems, discounted cash flow modeling with explicit technology risk assumptions, or forward revenue multiples anchored to disclosed guidance—would be necessary to establish a supportable valuation range. The current dataset does not support quantitative triangulation. Further analysis would require either identification of additional comparable transactions or reliance on fundamental valuation methodologies independent of peer multiples.
